evidence: packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:14 `value = value || []` reassigns the local destructured parameter binding; it does not mutate the props object or the parent's array. All updates go through copies (`[...value]` at lines 32, 40, 66, 85) before setValue. The same idiom is used in the existing packages/features/form-builder/Components.tsx:237 and :338. That existing code really does mutate the array in place (value[index]=..., value.splice); the new component fixes this.

apps/web/components/booking/BookingListItem.tsx:194 action id is 'add_members', but the feature adds guests (label t('additional_guests')). packages/ui/components/table/TableActions.tsx:61,85 render action.id as data-testid, so the menu item and the dialog submit button (apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:98 data-testid='add_members') get the same test id. That is ambiguous for e2e selectors. Renaming (for example 'add_guests' for the action and 'add_guests_submit' for the button) is cheap. It has no runtime effect.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 computes isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...). packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:264-284 shows isTeamAdmin already matches role ADMIN OR OWNER, and :286-295 shows isTeamOwner matches OWNER only. The conjunction therefore reduces to 'is owner'. The reviewer is wrong that it is impossible: owners pass both checks. They are right that team ADMINs who are not owners are rejected (unless they are the organizer or an attendee). Fix: use isTeamAdmin alone, or use ||.

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:33 sets the isInvalidEmail state to true only in handleAdd (line 57). It is reset only by the Cancel button (line 91). setMultiEmailValue is passed straight to MultiEmail (line 74) without clearing the flag, and onSuccess (lines 37-41) does not reset it either. After a failed attempt, the error banner stays visible while the user edits, and it is still showing when the dialog is reopened after a successful add or after closing via onOpenChange. This is a minor UX problem.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541 compares newGuests.includes(attendee.email). In addGuests.handler.ts:83-104, new attendees are created with `email: guest` exactly as the user supplied it, with no normalization by Prisma or the handler. The newly stored attendee email therefore matches the guest string byte-for-byte, and new guests do get AttendeeScheduledEmail. The real related bug is different: addGuests.handler.ts:168 passes `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`. An input email that exactly matches an existing attendee is filtered from insertion, but that existing attendee then receives a fresh AttendeeScheduledEmail.

addGuests.handler.ts:74-78 uses `guest === attendee.email`, which is case-sensitive. The client check in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29 (a Set) is also case-sensitive. An attendee 'User@Example.com' plus input 'user@example.com' creates a duplicate attendee record and sends extra invitations, because email addresses are effectively case-insensitive. Fix: compare with toLowerCase() on both sides.

packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:26 uses key={index}. Each EmailField is fully controlled (value={field}, line 29), and all state lives in the parent array. When an item is removed, the remaining inputs therefore re-render with the correct values, and the state-mismatch bug the reviewer describes does not occur for values. Only DOM-level state such as focus or cursor position can shift. The list also has no stable id (duplicate or empty strings are possible), so the value can't serve as a key either. The existing form-builder MultiEmail (packages/features/form-builder/Components.tsx:249) uses the same pattern. Low impact.

addGuests.handler.ts:167-171 catches the error and logs only 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails', discarding err. The point is valid: the cause is lost. However, the pattern is copied from the existing editLocation.handler.ts:134-141, which does the same thing, so it is consistent with neighbouring code. A cheap improvement is to include err, or to use the @calcom/lib/logger already imported in editLocation.handler.ts:5.

addGuests.handler.ts:70-72 lowercases blacklistedGuestEmails, but line 77 checks `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` with the raw guest. 'Blocked@X.com' bypasses a blacklist entry 'blocked@x.com'. The canonical implementation in packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:736-745 lowercases the guest (and also applies extractBaseEmail) before comparing. This is a security/abuse-control bypass.

AddGuestsDialog.tsx:32 initializes the field list to [''] (one empty email field), and handleAdd (lines 49-58) validates without filtering out blanks. Clicking Add immediately, though, makes z.string().email() fail and shows 'Emails must be unique and valid'. That is reasonable feedback, not a crash or a bad request. The real friction is that a trailing blank row added with 'Add another' blocks submission of otherwise valid emails. Filtering empty strings before validating would improve UX.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:525-550 sendAddGuestsEmails takes no eventTypeMetadata and sends host and attendee emails unconditionally. The sibling sendLocationChangeEmails (email-manager.ts:495-523) and most others (e.g. :89-133, :187-215, :477-493) gate on eventTypeDisableHostEmail / eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail (:81-88). The handler has booking.eventType (it includes eventType at addGuests.handler.ts:32), and editLocation.handler.ts:135-138 passes booking.eventType.metadata. Event types that have disabled standard emails (for example via workflows) would still get these emails.
